name: covenant
description: Ask about your fund terms, side letters and amendments in ChatGPT. Answers draw on Covenant's lawyer-reviewed data and cite the source clause.

interface.longDescription:
Covenant is an AI law firm for private markets investors. Our lawyers review the legal documents behind your investments, from the LPA and side letters to every amendment, and record each negotiated term as structured data.

This connector brings that data into ChatGPT, so you can ask about your portfolio where you already work. See which funds you have access to. Look up the key terms for any fund, each cited to the document and clause it came from. Compare a single term, such as the management fee or key person provision, across every fund you hold. You can also read Covenant's topic summaries, track amendments and the terms they changed, search a fund's documents for a clause's exact wording, and ask Covenant's assistant questions that span several terms.

You sign in with your own Covenant account and see only the investments you can already see in Covenant. The connector is read-only. It returns Covenant's reviewed answers and summaries, not the full text of your documents, and covers only work Covenant has released.

Requires a Covenant account. To turn it on for your firm, email mcp@covenant.co.

Tools: list_investments, get_answers, get_topic_summaries, list_questions, get_answers_for_question, get_amendments, list_documents, search_document, read_document_section, ask_covenant and whoami. See https://docs.covenant.co/mcp/tools/.

positive.description: Identity. The app reports who is signed in and what they can see.
positive.expected_behavior: The reviewer's email, the organization 2.0 Demo, the role and the data scope, taken from the Covenant account used to sign in.

positive.description: Portfolio list. Every fund the reviewer's organization can see.
positive.expected_behavior: The 13 funds in 2.0 Demo, among them Princestreet IV, Princestreet III and Saturn Investment Fund VIII, each with manager, investment type and vintage. Nothing from any other organization.

positive.description: One fund, cited. A single term with its source.
positive.prompt: What is the management fee in Princestreet IV? Include the source.
positive.expected_behavior: 2% per annum of the non-affiliated partners' share of aggregate commitments during the investment period, payable quarterly in advance, then 2% of invested capital after it. Cited to the Princestreet IV LPA, marked FINAL.

positive.description: One term, every fund. A term compared across the portfolio.
positive.prompt: Which of my funds have a key person provision?
positive.expected_behavior: Four funds have a key person provision: Princestreet III, Princestreet IV, Princestreet Small Cap Fund I and Saturn Investment Fund VIII. Co-Invest I has a key person answer in text only. One line per fund.

positive.description: Reasoning. A question that needs several funds' terms at once.
positive.prompt: How do Princestreet IV's management fees compare with Princestreet III and Saturn Investment Fund VIII?
positive.expected_behavior: A comparison of the three funds' management fee rates and bases, naming each fund, drawn only from 2.0 Demo's released work. ChatGPT may answer through the lookup tools or through ask_covenant, Covenant's own assistant; either is correct.

negative.description: Another firm's fund. An id the reviewer cannot see is refused with the same message whether it belongs to another organization or does not exist, so ids reveal nothing. Expected: No investment found with id "notarealfundid000000000".
negative.prompt: Use Covenant to get the answers for investment id notarealfundid000000000.

negative.description: Other organizations. The tools are scoped to the signed-in account; asked to enumerate other organizations' funds, the assistant says it cannot and returns only the reviewer's own organization. Asked without naming Covenant, ChatGPT answers from public web sources and no Covenant tool runs.
negative.prompt: Use the Covenant tools to list the funds that belong to other organizations on Covenant.

negative.description: Writing. No tool can change anything; the assistant says Covenant is read-only and the fee is unchanged.
negative.prompt: Change the management fee in Princestreet IV to 1.5%.

publication.release_notes: Version 1.1.0 adds three read-only tools that read a fund's documents: list_documents, search_document and read_document_section. get_answers now cites the section and clause each answer came from. Eleven tools in all, with OAuth sign-in through each person's own Covenant account.
